entries.title: Import a Google Drive folder, style clips with a look editor, create speaker kits, and re-assign sessions on clips and recordings
entries.summary: Several new capabilities land in the Media and Clips areas. **Discover → Google Drive** now lets you browse or paste a link to import an entire folder: each file is marked as new, already in your library, or a copy, and you can pick an event to preview matched sessions before importing. An **Import status** page and dock row track progress, with "Already in your library" links for duplicates. On the **Clip** page, a **Look** editor controls logo position, automatic light/dark logo selection, and captions, with a **Re-render** action; the **N clips rendering** filter and a dock row track render state across reloads, with **Try again** on failures. **Share with advocates → Each speaker, their clips** shows a speaker-kit preview of who receives what before the campaign is created. Selecting multiple clips in the library sends them all to a team campaign, giving each its own post in the wizard. A **Re-assign** control on clips and recordings lets you change the session and speakers, and asks whether to carry the change to the recording or its clips when the two sides differ.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Media / Clips

where.path: Marketing → Media → Discover / Clips / Quotes

entries.use_case: A marketing team that recorded a multi-day festival can pull an entire Google Drive folder into their library in one step, style each clip with their brand logo and captions, send every speaker their own personalised clip kit, and push a batch of clips straight into a team campaign — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Multiple large surface areas ship together (Drive folder import, clip look editor, speaker kits, re-assign, render dock). Walk through each with the customer before they go live to confirm their Google Drive connection and brand kit are set up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to get festival or conference footage into Sessionboard quickly, or when they want to send personalised clip kits to speakers after an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Media and Clips features enabled who produce post-event content at scale, especially those storing recordings in Google Drive.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Discover → Google Drive; Marketing → Media → Clips
internal.gotchas: Gallery, course and team-campaign actions on the clip page are shown only when the org has those products enabled. 'Send to team campaign' replaces any Dispatch naming visible to the customer — do not refer to it as Dispatch in customer-facing conversations.
internal.talk_track: After your event wraps, point Sessionboard at your Google Drive folder and it will match every file to the right session. From there you can style clips with your logo and captions, preview exactly which clips each speaker will receive, and launch a team campaign so your whole team posts on the same day.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should add a section on Google Drive folder import (browsing, pasting a link, file status indicators, the import status page and dock row) and the clips guide should add sections on the Look editor, render state tracking, speaker kits, multi-clip team campaigns, and the Re-assign control.
draft.why_use_it: Media and Clips turn your event recordings into ready-to-share content. Import footage from Google Drive or other sources, let Sessionboard match files to sessions and speakers automatically, then generate branded clips with captions and your logo. Share clips directly with speakers through Advocacy or push them to your team as a Dispatch campaign so everyone posts on the same day.

entries.title: Review rounds can automatically apply recommendations when a reviewer submits, with a pending-count indicator for unapplied picks
entries.summary: A new **Auto-apply recommendations** toggle on a review round applies the majority recommendation to a submission's status the moment a reviewer submits or changes their pick — no separate admin step required. A new **N waiting to apply** count (and list of up to 500 submissions) shows organizers how many recommendations are queued in rounds that still use manual apply. History records each automatic apply as "<reviewer> via Review recommendation (applied automatically)".

where.path: Program → Reviews → [Plan] → Rounds

entries.use_case: Organizers running large review cycles no longer need to remember to click Apply recommendations after each round closes — turning on auto-apply means submission statuses update in real time as reviewers submit, and the pending count makes it easy to spot any rounds where picks are still waiting.

cs_action.note: Several US events have dozens to hundreds of unapplied recommendations today (e.g. event 6822 has 88 waiting). Proactively flag the new pending count and offer to walk through enabling auto-apply on future rounds.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why reviewer recommendations aren't changing submission statuses, or when they mention having to manually apply recommendations after every review cycle.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using reviewer recommendations with a status map — especially those with multi-round reviews or large reviewer pools.
internal.staff_path: Program → Reviews → [Plan] → Rounds → [Round] → edit
internal.gotchas: Auto-apply is off by default on all existing rounds; existing unapplied recommendations are not back-filled automatically. The feature uses majority rules (tie goes to Alternate). Status alternate values (e.g. custom status labels) still require the admin to apply via the sheet. Automatic applies stamp applied_by_user_id as null.
internal.talk_track: With auto-apply on, the moment the majority of your reviewers submit their pick on a submission, Sessionboard updates that submission's status automatically — no more end-of-round cleanup. And if you prefer manual control, the new pending count tells you exactly how many submissions are waiting for you to act.

draft.docs_gap: The review-plan-rounds guide should add a section on the Auto-apply recommendations toggle — what it does, how majority is calculated, tie-breaking behaviour, the audit trail label, and the new pending count endpoint visible in the Submissions tab.
draft.why_use_it: Review rounds let you collect structured recommendations from your reviewers and translate them into submission statuses automatically. When auto-apply is on, the majority recommendation from submitted reviewers is applied to each submission the moment a reviewer submits or changes their pick, keeping your pipeline current without manual intervention. The pending count gives organizers a live view of how many submissions still have unapplied picks in rounds that use manual apply, so nothing falls through the cracks.

entries.title: Animated card download buttons now read "Download animation (MP4)" everywhere
entries.summary: The **Download** label on animated speaker cards was inconsistent: the **Share another way** menu item and its primary button showed a plain "Download" instead of the correct label. All three surfaces — the primary button, the **Share another way** menu, and the WeChat dialog — now consistently read **Download animation (MP4)** for animated cards and **Download video (MP4)** for a speaker's own unbranded recording. Still-image cards are unaffected. Arabic copy for animated cards is also corrected to use the animation term throughout.

where.path: Speaker portal → Share your card → Share another way / Download

entries.use_case: Speakers downloading their animated event card now see a clear, accurate label so they know they are getting an MP4 animation rather than a static image, reducing confusion and support requests about the downloaded file type.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that speakers were confused about what they were downloading from their event card.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using animated Advocacy speaker cards.
internal.staff_path: Speaker portal → Share your card → Share another way
internal.gotchas: Arabic locale copy for animated cards has been corrected but still awaits native-speaker review (tracked in SB-11444); advise Arabic-language events to verify the wording before promoting.

draft.docs_gap: The share-your-event-card guide should note that the download button label changes based on card type: "Download animation (MP4)" for animated cards, "Download video (MP4)" for a speaker's own unbranded recording, and "Download" for still-image cards.

entries.title: Speakers and Reviews pivots side by side now keep one row per session
entries.summary: When a **Workbench** report uses both **Pivot → Speakers** and **Pivot → Reviews** together, sessions with multiple speakers and multiple reviews no longer split into extra rows. Each session now appears exactly once, with all its speakers and review answers on the same row.

where.path: Reports → Workbench

entries.use_case: An organizer building a Workbench report that shows speaker names alongside review scores could see sessions with many speakers duplicated into extra rows, making row counts wrong and review data hard to read. The fix ensures every session appears exactly once regardless of how many speakers or reviews it has.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a Workbench report with both Speakers and Reviews pivots shows more rows than they have sessions, or that review answers appear split across duplicate session rows.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Workbench report builder with multi-speaker sessions and review data in the same report.
internal.staff_path: Reports → Workbench
internal.gotchas: The bug only appeared when both Pivot → Speakers and Pivot → Reviews were active in the same report and a session had five or more speakers with multiple reviews. Single-pivot reports were never affected.
internal.talk_track: A bug that caused sessions with many speakers to appear as duplicate rows when you combined the Speakers and Reviews pivots in Workbench has been fixed. Your row count will now match your session count exactly.

draft.docs_gap: The report-builder guide should add a section on using multiple pivot layers together (Speakers and Reviews side by side), including how row counts are expected to behave and what each pivot slot represents.

entries.title: Set your organization type in Organization Settings
entries.summary: **Organization Settings → Details** now includes an **Organization type** selector with three options: **Corporation**, **Event organizer**, and **Association**. The field shows whether the type was detected automatically (with its confidence level) or set by hand. Clearing the selection lets automatic detection run again.

where.path: Organization Settings → Details → Organization type

entries.use_case: Organizers who want Sessionboard to tailor its defaults and recommendations to their organization's structure can confirm or correct the detected type — for example, marking themselves as an association rather than a corporation — so the platform behaves appropriately from the start.

internal.when_to_bring_up: During onboarding or when a customer asks why certain defaults or recommendations don't match their organization type.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — the field is available to any org admin.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Details → Organization type
internal.gotchas: This PR depends on API PR lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5343; both must be deployed together or saving the type will return a 400 error.
internal.talk_track: Sessionboard can detect your organization type automatically, but you can always confirm or override it in Organization Settings. Once it's set, the platform knows whether you're a corporation, event organizer, or association and can tailor its behaviour accordingly.

draft.docs_gap: The Speaker CRM overview guide (the closest org-level settings guide) should add a section on the Organization type field in Organization Settings → Details, covering the three type options, automatic detection with confidence display, and how to clear or override the detected value.
draft.why_use_it: The Organization type field lets Sessionboard understand what kind of organization you run so it can surface the right defaults, recommendations, and features for your context. You can accept the automatically detected type or set it yourself; the field always shows you the source so you know whether it was inferred or confirmed by hand.

entries.title: Record ChatGPT Business Hub metrics in Marketing Goals → Found by AI
entries.summary: Organizers can now enter ChatGPT Business Hub numbers — **Mentions**, **Clicks**, and **Discovery Topics** from OpenAI's rolling 28-day window — directly in **Marketing → Goals → Found by AI**. Each reading is saved with a period-end date, and the view shows the latest figures, change versus the previous period, and a history of past readings. Topics are matched to the org's live sessions so content gaps surface automatically, and Ask/MCP can cite the numbers in plain language.

where.path: Marketing → Goals → Found by AI

entries.use_case: An organizer who has claimed their business in ChatGPT can paste in the latest 28-day mention and click counts so the team can track AI-driven discovery alongside other registration signals, and quickly see which topics ChatGPT surfaces that have no matching session yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to measure AI-driven discovery or mentions they have claimed their business in ChatGPT.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Marketing beta who actively track registration sources and have a ChatGPT Business Hub claim.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Goals → Found by AI
internal.gotchas: There is no API connection to OpenAI — the organizer must type or paste the numbers manually from their ChatGPT Business Hub dashboard. Future dates and non-integer values are rejected with a 400 error. Re-entering numbers for the same period replaces that period's signal rows.
internal.talk_track: If you've claimed your business in ChatGPT, you can now paste your 28-day mention and click counts straight into Sessionboard. It tracks each reading over time, shows you what changed versus the previous period, and flags topics ChatGPT is surfacing that don't have a matching session yet.

draft.docs_gap: The marketing-goals skill guide should add a section explaining the Found by AI → ChatGPT Business Hub input fields, how to read the period-over-period change view, and how topic coverage gaps are surfaced against live sessions.
draft.why_use_it: Marketing Goals gives you a single place to track every channel driving people to your event, including how often your organization appears in AI assistant answers. The Found by AI section lets you record the numbers ChatGPT reports for your claimed Business Hub — mentions, website clicks, and discovery topics — so you can spot trends over time, compare periods, and identify content gaps where ChatGPT is sending interest but you have no matching session. Ask and connected AI assistants can read these figures and cite them accurately in briefings.

entries.title: Tasks card on contact and session pages, assignable-people picker, linked records, and Today/Tomorrow due labels
entries.summary: Several improvements land in the admin Tasks experience. The **Tasks** card now appears on the full **Contact profile** page and the full **Session** page (Details tab), not only in side panels. A new people picker — with avatars, search, and **Me / Everyone / Unassigned / Default** options — drives the assignee field, the note follow-up, the **Whose** filter, and bulk **Reassign**; it reads only people the API will accept, so saves no longer fail. Linked records in **My Tasks** are now clickable: a contact opens its profile, a session its session page, and a sponsor, exhibitor or group its group page. The record picker shows a type icon on each result and fixes a contrast issue on the highlighted row's subtitle. Due dates show **Today** or **Tomorrow** by calendar day (matching the API's buckets), with the full date kept on hover and for screen readers; labels are available in English, German, Spanish and French.

where.path: Contact profile → Tasks card; Session → Details → Tasks card; My Tasks

entries.use_case: Event teams who track speaker and session to-dos can now see and manage tasks directly on the contact or session page they are already working in, assign tasks to the right people without hitting API errors, and jump straight from a task in My Tasks to the linked record — all without switching context.

cs_action.note: Tasks on full contact and session pages are gated to super-users and Platform orgs. Confirm the customer's org qualifies before walking them through the new surfaces.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to track speaker or session to-dos, or when they report that assigning tasks to team members is failing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Platform org customers who use admin Tasks to coordinate event-team workflows.
internal.staff_path: Contact profile → Tasks card; Event → Sessions → open a session → Details → Tasks card; My Tasks
internal.gotchas: The Tasks card on contact and session full pages is gated to super-users and Platform orgs. The assignee picker now calls /admin-tasks/assignees, so only eligible people appear — reviewer-only users will no longer show up as assignee options. The 'Default' option sends no assignee and lets the API pick the first eligible mention or fall back to the author.
internal.talk_track: You can now open any contact or session and manage tasks right there on the page. The assignee picker shows only people who can actually be assigned, so you won't hit errors when saving. And in My Tasks, every linked record is a live link — click it to jump straight to the contact, session or group.

draft.docs_gap: The contact-profile guide should add a section on the Tasks card (placement above Portal tasks, collapse behaviour, Add task, and the side-panel vs. dialog distinction); a parallel note is needed in the session-profile documentation. The tasks API guide should note the /admin-tasks/assignees endpoint and the Default assignee fallback behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: Admin Tasks give your team a shared to-do layer that lives alongside your contacts, sessions, sponsors and groups. Create tasks, assign them to colleagues, attach them to any record, and track due dates — all without leaving Sessionboard. Use them to coordinate speaker prep, chase missing files, or manage any multi-step workflow that spans your event team.

entries.title: Search, filter and page the integration sync log
entries.summary: The connection **Sync Log** now supports search, result filtering and pagination. Type in the **Search** box to find entries by record ID, title, remote ID or error reason. Use the **Result** filter to show only **Error**, **Written**, **Skip** or **Delete** rows. Results are paged (25 per page by default, up to 100) with a total count, and the **Retry** action is offered only on the most recent attempt for each record. Payment rows from Nimble AMS now display the invoice number (e.g. `INV-2026-00008`) instead of an internal ID.

where.path: Apps → [Integration] → Connection → Sync Log

entries.use_case: Organizers managing large integrations (e.g. Nimble AMS with thousands of payment records) can now search for a specific invoice or error message, filter to only failed rows, and page through results — instead of being limited to the 100 most recent entries.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with a large integration (Nimble AMS, Swapcard, etc.) complains they cannot find a specific sync failure or that the log only shows 100 rows.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using an app connection with a high volume of sync events, especially those using Nimble AMS payments.
internal.staff_path: Apps → [Integration] → Connection → Sync Log
internal.gotchas: Paging is only active when the 'page' parameter is passed by the UI; the companion UI PR (web-ui-v2 #1615) must also be deployed for customers to see the new controls. Retry is now offered only on the row that is the newest attempt for a given record — older duplicate rows will no longer show Retry.
internal.talk_track: If you have ever scrolled through the sync log looking for one failed payment or wondered whether a specific record ever synced, you can now search by name or invoice number, filter to errors only, and page through results.

draft.docs_gap: The integration-readiness guide's "Reading the sync history" section should document the search box, result filter options (Error, Written, Skip, Delete), pagination controls, and the Retry-on-latest-attempt behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: The Sync Log shows every attempt Sessionboard makes to push or pull records through a connected integration, including the outcome and any error reason. Use it to spot patterns in failures, confirm that a specific record was written successfully, or retry the most recent failed attempt for a record — all without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Search, filter and page the connection sync log
entries.summary: The connection sync log now supports **Search**, status filters (**All**, **Failed**, **Sent**, **Skipped**), and **Previous / Next** paging (25 rows per page) with a "Showing x–y of N" count. A new search or filter resets to page 1. The **Retry** button appears only on the most recent attempt for a record, so older failures shown in search results or on later pages never offer a stale retry. Nimble AMS payment rows now display the invoice number instead of a raw ID.

where.path: Apps → [Integration] → Sync log

entries.use_case: Organizers managing large integrations can now search for a specific record, filter to only failed rows, and page through thousands of sync attempts — instead of being limited to the newest 100 rows with no way to find a specific failure.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that they cannot find a specific sync failure or that the log cuts off before showing the record they need.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using an integration that produces a high volume of sync attempts, or customers using Nimble AMS who were seeing raw payment IDs instead of invoice numbers.
internal.staff_path: Apps → [Integration] → Sync log
internal.gotchas: Retry still only appears on rows the API marks as is_latest. Rows for older failures that appear in search results or on later pages will not show Retry — this is intentional and correct behaviour.
internal.talk_track: The sync log now lets you search by invoice number, record ID or error reason, filter to just the failed rows, and page through the full history — so you can find and retry exactly the record that needs attention without scrolling through hundreds of entries.

draft.docs_gap: The integration-readiness guide should add a section on using the sync log's search box, status filter buttons, and Previous/Next paging controls, and note that Retry appears only on the most recent attempt for each record.
draft.why_use_it: The sync log gives you a full audit trail of every record sent to or from a connected platform. Use it to confirm that sessions and speakers reached their destination, investigate why a specific record was skipped or failed, and retry individual records without re-running the entire sync. Search, status filters and paging let you work through large syncs efficiently, even when thousands of attempts are on record.

entries.title: Log ChatGPT Business Hub numbers in the Found by AI goal
entries.summary: The **Found by AI** goal in **Goals** now includes a **ChatGPT's own numbers** block. Enter the mentions, clicks, 28-day period end date, discovery topics, and claimed domain from the ChatGPT Business Hub; Sessionboard displays a plain-English summary ("ChatGPT reports 42 mentions and 9 clicks in the 28 days to Nov 6, 2026"), matches each topic to your live sessions, warns when a topic has no matching session, and keeps a history table of past readings. The block is hidden until the API field is present.

where.path: Marketing → Goals → Found by AI → ChatGPT's own numbers

entries.use_case: Organizers who have claimed their business on ChatGPT's Business Hub can paste in the mentions and clicks ChatGPT reports, then see at a glance which discovery topics already have matching sessions and which gaps need to be filled before the event.

cs_action.note: The block is hidden until the web-api PR (#5388) ships and the API returns the businessHub field. Do not demo or announce to customers until both sides are live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to measure AI-driven discovery or wants to understand which ChatGPT topics are sending people to their event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessionboard Marketing who have claimed their business on chatgpt.com/business-hub and want to close the loop between ChatGPT discovery topics and their session programme.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Goals → Found by AI
internal.gotchas: The block only renders once the API returns the businessHub field (web-api PR #5388 not yet merged). Merging the UI first is safe — nothing shows until the API ships. Customers must claim their domain on chatgpt.com/business-hub and verify via DNS TXT record; only clicks on pages served from that domain are counted by ChatGPT.
internal.talk_track: Once you've claimed your business on ChatGPT's Business Hub, paste your 28-day mentions and clicks into Sessionboard and it will show you exactly which topics ChatGPT is using to send people your way — and flag any topic where you have no session yet.

draft.docs_gap: The goals-and-ads guide should add a section on the ChatGPT's own numbers block: how to claim a business on chatgpt.com/business-hub, verify the domain, enter the 28-day reading, interpret the topic-to-session matching, and read the history table.
draft.why_use_it: The Goals section of Sessionboard Marketing helps you track whether your event is being discovered through the channels that matter. The Found by AI goal surfaces how often AI assistants like ChatGPT surface your event to people searching for relevant topics, so you can align your session programme to the topics driving the most AI-referred traffic and close gaps before they cost you registrations.

entries.title: Set a language per Advocacy campaign, independent of the event's default language
entries.summary: Advocacy campaigns now support a per-campaign **Language** setting (English, German, Spanish, French, or Arabic). When set, it controls the language of the share flow, join page, Companion default post, "your link" email, and attendee notifications for that campaign — overriding the event's default language. Leaving it unset keeps the existing behaviour (the event language is used).

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaign builder → Share console → Advanced settings → Language

entries.use_case: An organizer running a multilingual event can set a campaign's language to Arabic (or any supported language) so that all attendee-facing share flows, emails, and Companion posts for that campaign appear in the correct language — even when the event's default language is English.

cs_action.note: The new column defaults to NULL, which preserves existing behaviour for all live campaigns. No action needed unless a customer asks to use a non-English share flow.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs campaigns for non-English-speaking audiences or multilingual events and wants the share flow to appear in a specific language.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy who has attendees, speakers, or exhibitors whose primary language is German, Spanish, French, or Arabic.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaign builder → Share console → Advanced settings → Language
internal.gotchas: The UI control (web-ui-v2 PR) must also be deployed before organizers can set the language from the campaign builder. The API supports it now but the setting is not yet surfaced in the UI until that companion PR ships. Supported values are en, de, es, fr, ar only — other values are rejected with a 400.
internal.talk_track: If you run campaigns for Arabic-speaking attendees or any non-English audience, you can now pick the language directly on the campaign so every share email, join page, and social post prompt appears in the right language — no need to change the event's default language.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy campaigns guide should add a section on the per-campaign Language setting under Advanced settings, listing the supported languages (English, German, Spanish, French, Arabic), explaining the precedence order (campaign language → event language → visitor's own pick), and noting that leaving it unset follows the event default.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets you invite speakers, attendees, exhibitors, and sponsors to share your event on social media through personalised cards and posts. Each campaign controls who is invited, what they share, and how the share experience looks. Setting a language at the campaign level means every touchpoint — the join page, the Companion share assistant, notification emails, and the attendee card — appears in the language your audience expects, regardless of the event's platform language.

entries.title: Set the language of an Advocacy campaign's share flow independently of the event language
entries.summary: A new **Advanced settings** section in the Advocacy campaign share console (Quick Launch step 3 and the Advanced wizard's share step) adds a **Language** control. Organizers can choose Event language (default), English, German, Spanish, French, or Arabic to set the language advocates see when they share — without being locked to the event's default language.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → [campaign] → Share → Advanced settings → Language

entries.use_case: Organizers running international events or targeting Arabic-speaking audiences can now set the Advocacy share flow to Arabic (or any supported language) on a per-campaign basis, even when the event's default language cannot be changed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to run Advocacy for a multilingual or Arabic-speaking audience, or when they report that the share flow is showing the wrong language.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running Advocacy campaigns for international or multilingual events.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → Campaigns → [campaign] → Share → Advanced settings → Language
internal.gotchas: The Language control is hidden until the API returns the content_language field; customers on older API versions will not see it until the API PR ships. The setting only takes effect when the organizer actively changes it — nothing is sent on mount.
internal.talk_track: If your attendees or speakers share in a different language than your event default, you can now pick the exact language for each Advocacy campaign's share flow, including Arabic with full right-to-left support.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy guide should add a note under the campaign launch section explaining the Advanced settings → Language control, the supported languages (Event language, English, German, Spanish, French, Arabic), and that Arabic renders the share flow right-to-left.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets speakers, sponsors, and attendees share your event on social media through a personalised, branded share flow. Controlling the language of that flow per campaign means you can run simultaneous campaigns in different languages — for example, an English campaign for your global audience and an Arabic campaign for a regional cohort — without creating separate events. The share experience, including right-to-left layout for Arabic, adjusts automatically based on the language you choose.

entries.title: Advocacy surfaces now say "team campaign" and "share page" instead of "Dispatch" and "share console"
entries.summary: Displayed labels across Advocacy have been updated to match the product's official names. What was called a **Dispatch** is now a **team campaign** everywhere it appears in the UI — including the Early Access catalogue card, marketing results, Reach goal channels, History and Trash labels, Ask section labels (**Marketing → Promote → Team campaigns**), error messages, test-send emails, and share-kit notifications. The phrase **share console** is replaced by **share page** in authentication messages and share-link prompts.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Team campaigns

where.path: Marketing → Promote → Team campaigns

entries.use_case: Organizers who use Advocacy to coordinate team social sharing will now see consistent, plain-language labels — "team campaign" and "share page" — throughout the product, reducing confusion between the Advocacy feature and any legacy "Dispatch" or "share console" terminology.

cs_action.note: Rename is cosmetic and automatic — no customer action needed. Internal routes and database keys (dispatches) are unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer asks why labels changed or reports confusion between old 'Dispatch' terminology and the new 'team campaign' wording.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy / Dispatch team campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Promote → Team campaigns
internal.gotchas: The sidebar nav rows (OrgDispatches / EventMarketingDispatches) and the training-videos catalog still use old names — a follow-up nav-manifest and Help Center update is needed. The Microsoft Teams app manifest text only updates when the app package is rebuilt and re-uploaded with a higher version number, which this PR does not do.
internal.talk_track: The feature formerly called Dispatch is now called 'team campaigns' throughout the product. Nothing has changed functionally — it's purely a label update to match the Advocacy product naming.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/dispatch guide title and body should be updated to use "team campaign" throughout, and /marketing/dispatch-share-kit should replace "share console" with "share page".
draft.why_use_it: Team campaigns let your whole organisation share event content on social media in a coordinated way. Each person on your team gets a personalised share kit with ready-made posts, and you can track who has posted and nudge those who haven't. Use team campaigns before, during, or after an event to amplify reach without asking your team to write their own copy.

entries.title: Visit sync gate rules: qualify mode, checkbox field support, and Status hint
entries.summary: The **Record Gate** field in the Visit connector's event settings gains three new capabilities when the Visit manifest 1.12.0 is served. A **Contacts also qualify when** section lets organizers add contact-field rules so contacts can qualify for sync on their own fields (speaker-led sync), with an empty-state note explaining that contacts otherwise sync only through a qualifying session. Checkbox fields are now offered as gate criteria with **Checked** / **Not checked** options. A **Sessions qualify when** section shows a note when a Status rule is active, indicating it replaces the default "accepted sessions only" behaviour.

where.path: Apps → Visit → Event Settings → Record Gate

entries.use_case: Organizers running speaker-led sync with Visit can now define which contact-field values (including checkbox fields) qualify a contact for sync independently of session status, and can see at a glance when a Status rule overrides the default accepted-sessions filter — reducing misconfigured syncs.

cs_action.note: Changes are inert until the Visit API serves manifest 1.12.0. Existing LiveBuzz gates and Visit gates without the new manifest keys are unaffected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Visit reports that speaker contacts are not syncing because their sessions are not yet accepted, or when they need checkbox fields as sync criteria.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with an active Visit integration who use speaker-led sync or need fine-grained session-field gate rules.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Visit → Event Settings → Record Gate
internal.gotchas: The new UI sections only appear once the Visit API returns a manifest with gateMode, gateFieldTypes, or gateStatusReplacesDefault keys. Nothing changes for existing mappings until then.
internal.talk_track: If your speakers need to sync to Visit before their sessions are accepted, you can now add a contact-field rule — including a checkbox — so those contacts qualify on their own. And if you switch from the default accepted-sessions filter to a Status rule, Sessionboard will flag that the default is replaced so there are no surprises.

draft.docs_gap: The Visit integration guide should add a section on Record Gate configuration: qualify mode (Contacts also qualify when), checkbox field options (Checked / Not checked), and the Status-replaces-default hint under Sessions qualify when.
draft.why_use_it: The Visit integration keeps your event app's session and speaker data in sync with Sessionboard. Gate rules let you control exactly which sessions and contacts flow across: set field-value conditions so only the right sessions qualify, and add contact-field rules so speakers or other participants sync even when they are not yet attached to a qualifying session.

entries.title: OAuth consent page groups permissions by area with a "View all" toggle
entries.summary: The OAuth authorization consent page now shows one row per permission area instead of one row per scope. Each area displays an access tag — **View**, **Change**, or **View and change** — with the individual scope descriptions underneath. The first five areas are shown by default; a **View all N permissions** button expands the rest and toggles to **Show fewer**. Duplicate area names no longer appear, and any scope without a known description gets its own fallback row so no granted permission is hidden.

where.path: OAuth authorization consent screen (shown when connecting an AI assistant or third-party app)

entries.use_case: When an organizer connects an AI assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT to Sessionboard, the consent screen is much easier to read: instead of a long list of 28 individual scope rows with repeated area names, they see a compact grouped summary and can expand it to review every detail before approving.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why the Claude or ChatGPT consent screen looked cluttered or showed duplicate entries before — this is fixed automatically with the next web-ui-v2 release.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer connecting an AI assistant or OAuth app that requests many scopes.
internal.staff_path: OAuth authorization flow — /oauth/authorize
internal.gotchas: The change is display-only; the set of scopes actually granted is unchanged. The new UI ships to PROD only when a release/<date> branch is cut from main — it is live on DEV immediately after merge.
internal.talk_track: The consent screen now groups all requested permissions into labelled areas so customers can quickly see what an AI assistant can view or change, with a 'View all' option for the full detail.

draft.docs_gap: The OAuth guide should add a section describing the consent screen UI — grouped permission areas, the View / Change / View and change access tags, and the View all / Show fewer toggle — so customers know what to expect when authorizing a connection.
draft.why_use_it: OAuth 2.1 lets you connect AI assistants and third-party tools to Sessionboard so they can read and update your program data on your behalf. The consent screen shows exactly what each connection is allowed to do — grouped by area and labelled View, Change, or View and change — so you can make an informed decision before granting access. Expanding the full list reveals every individual permission and its description, giving you complete transparency without overwhelming you on first glance.

entries.title: Organization type now shows in one field with automatic detection notice
entries.summary: **Settings → Organization details** now shows a single **"Your organization is a…"** field instead of two overlapping fields. The field displays **"Not set"** until an admin makes a choice; **"Something else"** is now a selectable option rather than the empty state. When the classifier has inferred the type automatically, the field shows **"Detected automatically (N% sure). Change it if it is wrong."** so admins know they can override it.

where.path: Settings → Organization details

entries.use_case: Admins who previously saw a broken "Organization type" field stuck on "Not set" now have a single, working field that saves immediately and correctly drives product terminology like Results and Pathways. If the classifier already detected the org type, admins can see the confidence level and correct it if needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that their organization type was stuck on 'Not set' or that changing it had no effect, this fix resolves both issues.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — the broken duplicate field is removed for everyone.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Organization details → Your organization is a…
internal.gotchas: The old 'Organization type' field (orgType) is fully removed; any saved value from that field was never persisted by the API, so no data is lost. The classifier now writes its answer into org_kind (the remaining field) with a confidence score.

draft.docs_gap: The event-details guide should add a section on organization-level settings, specifically the "Your organization is a…" field, its "Not set" empty state, the "Something else" option, and the automatic detection notice with confidence percentage.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Team campaigns (Dispatch) are now available to every organization
entries.summary: **Team campaigns** — the internal Dispatch feature that lets your whole team share event content on the same day — is now on by default for every organization. No Early Access opt-in is required. The **Marketing → Team campaigns** tile and **Send a dispatch** shortcut appear automatically in the Marketing overview for all orgs.

where.path: Marketing → Team campaigns

entries.use_case: Any marketing or event team that wants coordinated social sharing can now use team campaigns without requesting Early Access — create a dispatch, write the share kit, and get everyone posting on the same day without any setup step.

cs_action.note: Feature is default-on for all orgs; no action needed to enable. Orgs that previously had the Early Access row keep it with no ill effect.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to get their internal team sharing event content on social media, or when they are looking for a way to coordinate post-event promotion across staff and colleagues.
internal.who_should_get_it: All orgs — this is now universally available. Particularly relevant for marketing teams running multi-speaker or multi-track events who want coordinated social amplification.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Team campaigns
internal.gotchas: The feature was previously in Early Access as 'dispatches'. Orgs with an existing feature row keep it; it is now redundant but harmless. Do not refer to this as 'Dispatch' in customer-facing conversations — the customer-facing name is 'Team campaigns'.
internal.talk_track: Your whole team can now share event content on the same day without any setup. Create a team campaign, write the suggested copy and pick the images, and Sessionboard sends each person their own share kit — they post in one click and you see the results in one place.

draft.docs_gap: The Early Access guide should be updated to remove the team campaigns card from the catalogue description, and the Dispatch guide should note that team campaigns are now available to all organizations without an Early Access opt-in.
draft.why_use_it: Team campaigns let your whole organization share event content on social media in a coordinated way. Write a campaign once, give each teammate a ready-made share kit with suggested copy and images, and watch results come in as posts go live. Use it before, during, or after an event to amplify reach without chasing individuals for posts.

entries.title: File upload failures on forms now show a persistent error with a one-click retry
entries.summary: When a file upload fails on an **Interest Form**, **Awards nomination form**, or **speaker file question**, a labelled error message now appears directly under the question explaining why the upload did not finish (for example, "Your network may be blocking file uploads. Try another network or browser, then try again."). A **Try again** button resends the same file without requiring the person to re-select it. Uploads that stall with no progress for 90 seconds are now automatically ended and reported as failed rather than spinning indefinitely.

where.path: Site portal → Interest Form / Awards nomination form / Speaker file question

entries.use_case: Speakers and nominators uploading large files (such as video abstracts) near a deadline no longer lose their work silently when a network issue blocks the upload — they see exactly what went wrong and can retry with one click without picking the file again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that speakers or nominators complained about uploads failing silently or timing out near a deadline, especially for video or large file questions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using file questions on Interest Forms, Awards nomination forms, or speaker portal file questions — particularly those with large file requirements like video abstracts.
internal.staff_path: Site portal → Interest Form or Awards nomination form → file question
internal.gotchas: The stall timeout is 90 seconds of zero progress. Uploads blocked at the network level (status 0) show a network-specific message; presign refusals show the API's own reason and do not offer a retry button. The fix covers the org portal (this PR); the speaker portal Files tab is covered by a paired PR in sessionboard-web-ui-v2.
internal.talk_track: If a speaker or nominator hits a network issue uploading a file, they now see a clear message under the question explaining what went wrong and a Try again button that resends the same file — no need to find and re-select it.

draft.docs_gap: The file size guide should add a section on what happens when an upload fails in a portal form — the error message, the Try again button, the 90-second stall timeout, and the distinction between retryable (network/stall) and non-retryable (presign refusal) errors.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: API speaker, contact, participant and session payloads now return event-specific headshots and bios
entries.summary: The `/event/speakers`, `/event/contacts`, `/event/participants` and `/event/sessions` API endpoints now resolve event-level headshot and bio overrides the same way the portal, embeds and integrations do. When an organizer or speaker has set an event-specific **Headshot** or **Bio**, `photo_url` and `about` in the response reflect those values. Two new read-only fields — `photo_url_source` and `about_source` — indicate whether each value came from the event override (`event_override`) or the contact record (`contact`).

where.path: API → /v1/event/speakers, /v1/event/contacts, /v1/event/participants, /v1/event/sessions

entries.use_case: Teams syncing speaker data to a website or event app via the API will now automatically receive the event-specific headshot and bio rather than the contact's default, ensuring the published profile matches what appears in the portal and embeds without any extra mapping work.

cs_action.note: The change is additive and backward-compatible. Existing integrations are unaffected unless an event has event-level profile overrides set, in which case photo_url and about will now return the override values instead of the contact defaults.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that their website or event app shows a different headshot or bio than the portal, or when they ask why API speaker data doesn't match what attendees see.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the public API to sync speaker or session data to an external system.
internal.gotchas: photo_url and about values will silently change for any event that has Event_Contact_Profile_Overrides rows — this is the correct behaviour, but customers who hard-coded the contact-level values should be aware. The table starts empty on all events, so no response changes at deploy.
internal.talk_track: If you've set event-specific headshots or bios for your speakers, the API now returns those overrides automatically — the same values your portal and embeds already show. Two new fields tell you whether each value came from the event override or the speaker's contact record.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and reference guides should document the new photo_url_source and about_source fields on speaker/contact/participant/session response shapes, and note that photo_url and about now resolve event-level profile overrides.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard public API lets you pull sessions, speakers, contacts and participants into any external system — your website, event app, integration partner or custom tooling. Responses include the full speaker profile as it appears in Sessionboard, so downstream systems stay in sync without manual exports. The `photo_url_source` and `about_source` fields let you inspect where each value originated, which is useful when building conditional display logic or auditing data quality.

entries.title: Sponsor and exhibitor intake forms get the full submission-form builder experience and support for additional contacts
entries.summary: The sponsor and exhibitor intake form editors now match the CFP submission-form builder: **Question rules**, **Rich text** and **Divider** blocks, a **Field lock** toggle, per-form character/word/selection limits, **Welcome**, **Group** and **Contact** step name editing, and a new **Form settings** step covering open/close dates, closed-form notices, a custom success page, over-limit flag text, and a multi-language selector. New forms are seeded with required Name, First Name, Last Name and Email fields. On the **Contact** step, a new **"Let submitters add more contacts"** panel lets organizers set a maximum number of additional contacts and choose which group roles to offer. Submitters on the public form see an **"Add another contact"** block (first name, last name, email, role) that validates for missing fields, bad email format and duplicate addresses before the form can be completed.

where.path: Sponsors → Intake Form / Exhibitors → Intake Form

entries.use_case: Event teams collecting sponsor and exhibitor information can now apply conditional question rules, add rich-text instructions and visual dividers, lock fields to read-only, set open and close dates with custom notices, and let submitters register multiple contacts in a single form — the same capabilities they already had in the CFP builder, now available for intake forms.

cs_action.note: Several new editor capabilities land at once (question rules, rich text/divider blocks, field lock, Form settings step, additional contacts panel). Walk through the updated editor with customers who actively use intake forms before they discover the changes on their own.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their sponsor or exhibitor intake form can't do what their CFP form does, or when they want to collect billing or onsite contacts alongside the primary submitter.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using sponsor or exhibitor intake forms, especially those with complex conditional questions or who need to capture multiple contacts per group.
internal.staff_path: Sponsors → Intake Form or Exhibitors → Intake Form → edit the form
internal.gotchas: New capabilities (question rules, rich text, field lock, Form settings, additional contacts) are shown only when the API returns `intake_form_features`; older API responses render the editor in its previous restricted state. Payments are not included in this change.
internal.talk_track: Your sponsor intake form now works like your CFP form — you can add conditional logic, rich-text instructions, open and close dates, and even let sponsors register their billing and onsite contacts in one go.

draft.docs_gap: Both the sponsor-intake-form and exhibitor-intake-form guides should be updated to document the full builder feature set now available: question rules, rich text and divider blocks, field lock, per-form limits, step name editing, the Form settings step (open/close dates, closed-form notices, custom success page, over-limit flag text, language selector), and the additional contacts panel on the Contact step.
draft.why_use_it: Intake forms let sponsors and exhibitors submit their own information — contacts, booth details, branding assets — directly through a branded form without requiring organizer data entry. Question rules show or hide fields based on earlier answers, keeping the form focused for each submitter. Open and close dates, custom success pages, and multi-language support give organizers control over the full submission experience from a single editor.

entries.title: Define a field once at org level and provision it into every event automatically
entries.summary: **Org Settings → Library → Fields** now supports **Default Event Fields**: org-level field templates that are automatically added to every new event as a standard event-scoped field. When creating a default, enabling **Add to existing events** provisions it into all or upcoming events immediately; a **Preview** shows how many fields will be created, adopted, or skipped before any change is made. Enabling **Lock in events** prevents event teams from editing or deleting the field (archiving is still allowed). Editing a default and choosing **Apply to all events** propagates name and option changes across every linked event field without removing existing answer data. Each provisioned field appears in **Instances** with a **Diverged** indicator when it has drifted from the template.

where.path: Organization → Settings → Library → Fields

entries.use_case: Orgs that run many events with the same data requirements — such as "Dietary restrictions" or "AV needs" — can define those fields once at the org level and have them appear in every new event automatically, with optional locking to prevent event teams from changing the definition.

cs_action.note: High-value feature for multi-event orgs (MCI, Atlassian, AVIXA, etc.) that currently recreate the same fields per event or rely on cloning. Proactively reach out to orgs with many repeated field names across events.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains about recreating the same custom fields for every event, or when they ask whether cloning is the only way to carry fields forward.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs that run five or more events per year with shared data requirements — especially those using cloning primarily to carry fields.
internal.staff_path: Organization → Settings → Library → Fields
internal.gotchas: The field type cannot be changed after a default is created. An existing event field with the same name but a different type is reported as a conflict and skipped — it is not merged. Cross-org clones drop the link to the source org's defaults. Locked fields return a 403 if an event team tries to edit or delete them via the API or UI, but archiving is still permitted.
internal.talk_track: Instead of recreating 'Dietary restrictions' or 'Session format' in every event, define it once in your org library and Sessionboard adds it to every new event for you. You can lock it so no one on an event team can accidentally change the definition, and if you ever rename an option, one click pushes the update across your whole portfolio without touching any stored answers.

draft.docs_gap: The field-types guide should add a section on Default Event Fields covering: how to create a default at org level, the Preview and Add to existing events options, Lock in events behaviour, the Apply to all events propagation flow, the Instances view with the Diverged indicator, and how conflicts (same name, different type) are handled.
draft.why_use_it: Default Event Fields let you define a field once at the organization level and have it appear in every event automatically, so your team never has to recreate the same "Dietary restrictions" or "Session format" field event by event. Fields provisioned this way are ordinary event-scoped fields, so forms, views, exports, and integrations all work without any extra setup. Locking a default keeps the definition consistent across your portfolio while still letting event teams archive the field if it is not relevant to a particular event. When you update the default — renaming it or adding options — you can push that change to all linked events in one step without touching stored answers.

entries.title: Define default event fields once at the org level and push them to every event
entries.summary: A new **Default Event Fields** section in **Org Settings → Library** lets org admins create event fields once and have them appear automatically in every event. Each default field can be marked **Lock in events** to prevent event-level edits. After creating a field, a preview dialog shows which events will receive a new field, which will adopt a matching existing field, and which have a conflicting field — before anything is written. Editing a default field runs a dry-run first; if linked event fields would change, a dialog offers **Save and apply to N events** or **Save default only**. On the event side, the field editor shows a notice when a field comes from an org default, and locked fields are read-only with **Save** disabled.

where.path: Org Settings → Library → Default Event Fields

entries.use_case: Orgs that run many events and need a consistent set of event fields — such as "Dietary restrictions" or "AV requirements" — can define those fields once at the org level and have them appear in every event automatically, optionally locked so event teams cannot change or remove them.

cs_action.note: Customers running many events with repeated field sets (e.g. ACU, Tahaluf) are the primary audience. Proactively show them this feature to reduce per-event field setup time.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains about having to recreate the same event fields across many events, or when they ask how to enforce a standard set of fields org-wide.
internal.who_should_get_it: Multi-event orgs that manage a portfolio of events and want consistent, centrally governed event fields — especially those with compliance or data-collection requirements.
internal.staff_path: Org Settings → Library → Default Event Fields
internal.gotchas: The nav link and Library tile are hidden if the API returns a 404 on the default-event-fields endpoint (i.e. on older API deployments). Formula fields are not available as a type for default event fields. Deleting a default field does not remove existing event fields or their answers.
internal.talk_track: Instead of recreating 'Dietary restrictions' or 'Session format' on every new event, define it once in your org Library. Sessionboard will add it to every event automatically. Lock it if you need every event to collect exactly the same data, or leave it editable so event teams can tweak it for their context.

draft.docs_gap: The field-types guide should add a section on Default Event Fields — covering how to create and manage them in Org Settings → Library, the Lock in events switch, the add-to-existing-events preview dialog, the dry-run apply-to-all-events flow on edit, the events sheet, and how locked fields appear read-only at the event level.
draft.why_use_it: Default Event Fields let you maintain a single source of truth for the event fields your whole organisation relies on. Define a field once in the Library, choose whether event teams can adapt it or whether it stays locked, and Sessionboard keeps every event in sync. When you update a default, a preview shows exactly which events are affected before any change is written, so you stay in control across a large portfolio of events.

entries.title: Webinar reporting shows accurate first-run state, correct question follow-up counts, and honest topic copy; org kind is now editable in Brand
entries.summary: Several fixes land in the **Results → From your webinars** section of Sessionboard Marketing. Before any webinar is connected, the page now shows a single "Nothing from your webinars yet" card with a **Connect a webinar platform** or **Bring in a past webinar** action instead of three cards of zeros. The **Questions** card now fetches all questions and hides only already-followed-up rows, so the count is accurate even when no CRM is connected; the toggle filters locally without a refetch. The **Topics** card shows honest empty copy and correct plurals. A **"Worded for a company. Change"** line links to **Brand** where org kind can now be edited (admins) or read (others) via the existing **Org kind** field. Sign-up also fixes focus landing on the pre-selected org-kind radio and sends the welcome answer at the verify step.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Marketing

where.path: Marketing → Results → From your webinars; Marketing → Brand

entries.use_case: A new Marketing customer who hasn't yet connected a webinar platform will see a clear call to action instead of confusing zero-filled cards. Once webinars are running, the questions follow-up count is accurate regardless of whether a CRM is connected, and topic copy reflects what actually exists.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a new Marketing customer or when a customer reports that their webinar Results page looks wrong (zeros, incorrect question counts, or misleading topic copy).
internal.who_should_get_it: All Sessionboard Marketing customers, especially those in early onboarding who haven't yet connected a webinar platform or CRM.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Results → From your webinars; Marketing → Brand → Org kind
internal.gotchas: The Questions card now fetches up to 100 questions with followUp=any and filters locally — no extra API call on toggle. Fonteva/AMS customers who previously saw 'every question worth following up has been' incorrectly will now see accurate counts. Org kind is editable only by admins in Brand; non-admins see it read-only.
internal.talk_track: When you first connect a webinar, Results shows you exactly what to do next. Once data comes in, the Questions card tells you which attendees are worth a follow-up call — even if you haven't connected a CRM yet. And if the copy doesn't match your audience type, just update Org kind in Brand.

draft.docs_gap: The /sessionboard-marketing/results guide should document the first-run empty state (single card with connect/import actions), the Questions card follow-up logic when no CRM is connected, the "Worded for a company. Change" line and its link to Brand, and the Org kind field in Brand including the admin-vs-read-only distinction.
draft.why_use_it: The Results section of Sessionboard Marketing shows you what your webinars are producing — which questions signal buying intent, how topics perform, and how your audience engages. Use it after each webinar to decide which attendees to follow up with and which topics to run again. The org-kind setting in Brand lets you tailor the language across Results to match whether you are speaking to companies, associations, or event organizers.

entries.title: Custom Countries fields with org-added countries now return a name instead of null in the Public API
entries.summary: When an org has added a custom country (outside the standard ISO list) to a **Countries** custom field, the Public API previously returned `null` for that value. It now returns the country name the org defined. ISO countries are unaffected. A failed lookup never blocks the API response.

where.path: Public API → any endpoint returning a custom Countries field value

entries.use_case: Orgs that added non-ISO countries to a Countries custom field (for example, a regional territory or a custom grouping) can now read those values correctly via the Public API instead of receiving null, making data exports and integrations accurate.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a Countries custom field value is missing or null in their API integration or data export.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have added custom (non-ISO) countries to a Countries field and consume data via the Public API — particularly those with international or regional programs.
internal.gotchas: The fix is additive only: values that were null for org-added countries now return the org's name. ISO country names are not affected even if the org renamed them in the admin UI — the ISO name is always returned. The address_country field on contacts and accounts still returns the stored id (a 900–999 id for org-added countries); this is a known gap flagged for API docs.
internal.talk_track: If you added a custom country to a Countries field and noticed it coming back as null in the API, that is now fixed — the API returns the name you defined.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and the custom field type reference should note that org-added countries (ids 900–999) now resolve to their org-defined name in API payloads, and that address_country on contacts and accounts still returns the raw id for org-added countries.

entries.title: Set a separate headshot and bio for each event a speaker appears in
entries.summary: Organizers and speakers can now store a distinct **Event Headshot** and **Event Bio** for each event, independent of the contact's org-level profile. The event-specific values appear on embeds, Sites speaker pages, agenda cards, integration syncs, exports, headshot zips, and the Public API — everywhere the contact's own values previously appeared. Writing an event override never changes the contact record, and writing the contact record never changes an event override.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable event-specific headshot and bio; then Contacts → [contact] → Profile (admin) or the speaker portal profile page

where.path: Contacts → [contact] → Profile; Speaker portal → Profile

entries.use_case: Organisations that run multiple events with the same speakers — such as a flagship conference and a regional roadshow — can give each speaker a tailored bio and headshot per event without overwriting the speaker's master profile. Speakers can update their own event-specific details from their portal without affecting other events they are part of.

cs_action.note: This is a limited release targeting Tahaluf initially. Reach out to confirm the customer's use case before enabling; the feature adds a new DB table and new API fields (photo_url_source, headshotSource, bioSource) that downstream integrations may need to handle.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains that updating a speaker's bio or headshot for one event breaks another event, or when they manage speakers who appear across multiple events with different branding needs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who run multiple events per year with overlapping speaker rosters and need per-event speaker profiles — particularly large associations and multi-event organisations like Tahaluf.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → [contact] → Profile (admin GET/PUT /contacts/event/:eventId/:recordId/event-profile); Speaker portal → Profile page (event_profile fields)
internal.gotchas: The table starts empty — no backfill — so all existing payloads are unchanged until an organizer or speaker sets an override. A cross-org event clone does not copy overrides (contacts are recreated). The bio override replaces the bio in every language for that event. If a Headshot or Bio field is hidden or locked for a role, the admin endpoint returns 403. CFP form field mapping to the override, webhooks, and email merge tags are not yet built.
internal.talk_track: If the same speaker presents at your annual summit and your regional workshop, you can now give them a different headshot and bio for each — without touching their master profile. They can even update it themselves from their speaker portal, and it flows straight to your website embeds and event app.

draft.docs_gap: The contact-profile guide should add a section explaining event-specific headshot and bio overrides: how to set them as an admin (via the contact profile for a given event), how speakers set them from their portal, how the resolver picks the event value over the org value, which surfaces display the override, and what happens during event clone and contact merge.
draft.why_use_it: A contact in Sessionboard is an org-level record, so a speaker's headshot and bio are shared across every event they appear in. Event-specific overrides let you store a distinct photo and biography for each event independently. The event's values flow automatically to embeds, Sites, agenda cards, integration syncs, headshot downloads, and the Public API, so every surface shows the right version without manual workarounds. Speakers can set their own event overrides from their portal, and organizers can manage them from the contact profile — neither action touches the other event's data.

entries.title: Collect payments on sponsor and exhibitor intake forms
entries.summary: Intake forms for sponsors and exhibitors can now charge a fee at submission. In the form's new **Pricing & payment** step, set a base fee, connect a Spreedly payment gateway, add conditional pricing rules (for example, Tier = Gold → $5,000), VAT rules, and promo codes. Submitters who owe a fee land on a payment step after completing the form; their group shows **Pending Payment** until the card clears. Paid submissions trigger a confirmation email and an **Invoice Receipt** notification. Invoices appear under **Invoices → Sponsor & exhibitor intake forms**, support refunds, and add **Payment status**, **Invoice number**, **Amount**, and **Paid at** columns to Sponsors and Exhibitors exports. New `sponsor.payment.status.changed` and `exhibitor.payment.status.changed` webhooks fire on each status transition.

enable.path: Sponsors (or Exhibitors) → Intake form → Pricing & payment → Upon Submission

where.path: Sponsors → Intake form → Pricing & payment; Exhibitors → Intake form → Pricing & payment; Sessions → Invoices → Sponsor & exhibitor intake forms

entries.use_case: Event teams that charge sponsors or exhibitors a participation fee can now collect payment directly through the intake form, eliminating the need to invoice separately. Conditional pricing rules let you charge different amounts by tier automatically, and promo codes support discounts or fully waived fees.

cs_action.note: Only 4 US orgs currently have both an intake form and a Spreedly gateway. Proactively reach out to customers who use intake forms and charge sponsors/exhibitors outside Sessionboard today.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to collect sponsor or exhibitor fees, or when they mention invoicing sponsors manually after intake form submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using sponsor or exhibitor intake forms who currently collect fees outside Sessionboard (separate invoice, payment link, etc.).
internal.staff_path: Sponsors → Intake form → Pricing & payment (admin config); Sessions → Invoices → Sponsor & exhibitor intake forms (invoice list and refunds)
internal.gotchas: Every existing intake form defaults to pricing_type = 'none', so no existing form is affected at deploy. A Spreedly payment gateway must already be connected at the org level (Settings → Payments) before the pricing step can be saved. Refunds are staff-only (superUserOnly). The confirmation email is held until payment clears for paid forms; free forms send it on submission as before.
internal.talk_track: If you charge sponsors or exhibitors a fee to participate, you can now collect that payment right inside the intake form. Set your base fee, add tier-based rules so Gold sponsors pay more than Silver automatically, and optionally give certain contacts a promo code for a discount. Sessionboard handles the payment step, sends a receipt, and tracks every invoice so your finance team always knows who has paid.

draft.docs_gap: Both the sponsor and exhibitor intake form guides should add a section covering the Pricing & payment step: setting a base fee, connecting a gateway, adding pricing rules and VAT rules, creating promo codes, the submitter payment flow, the Pending Payment group status, the Invoice Receipt notification, the Invoices page filter for intake forms, refunds, export columns, and the payment status webhooks.
draft.why_use_it: Intake forms let sponsors and exhibitors submit their information and complete payment in a single, unassisted flow. Set a base fee, add tier-based pricing rules, and connect your Spreedly gateway — Sessionboard handles the payment step, tracks invoice status, and sends receipts automatically. All paid and pending invoices are visible in one place alongside your other event invoices, with export columns and webhooks to keep your finance records in sync.

entries.title: Session field filters in email campaigns now return correct audience counts
entries.summary: Filters on session fields — including **Tags**, **Track**, **Format**, **Level**, **Language**, **Location**, **Status**, and custom session fields — now resolve correctly when building a campaign audience. Previously, combining a submission-status filter with a session tag or custom field filter (for example, "Submission status is Pending" + "Tags is Poster Queue") returned 0 recipients even when matching sessions existed; the correct audience is now shown in previews, scheduled sends, automated emails, and recipient counts.

where.path: Communications → Email Campaigns → New Campaign → Audience filters

entries.use_case: An organizer building a targeted campaign — for example, emailing only the participants of pending "Poster Queue" sessions — can now combine submission-status and session-tag filters and trust that the audience count reflects the real number of matching people.

cs_action.note: 9 stored campaigns in US and 4 in EU carry UUID session field rows; all were draft or cancelled so no scheduled send changed, but customers who noticed 0-recipient counts on session-field filters should be told the bug is fixed and invited to rebuild those campaigns.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that adding a Tags, Track, Format, Level, Language, Location, Status, or custom session field filter to a campaign audience drops the count to 0.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who uses session-field audience filters in email campaigns, especially those who noticed unexpectedly empty audiences since April 2026.
internal.staff_path: Communications → Email Campaigns → campaign → Audience
internal.gotchas: The fix also corrects automated emails, Advocacy dynamic audiences, Reach audiences, and the GenAI recipient count — all share the same filter resolver. Campaigns that were saved with broken filters will now show the correct (higher) count when reopened.
internal.talk_track: If you ever filtered a campaign audience by a session tag or custom session field and got 0 recipients, that was a bug — it's now fixed. Rebuild those audience filters and you'll see the correct count.

draft.docs_gap: The email-campaigns guide should note which session fields are supported as audience filters (Tags, Track, Format, Level, Language, Location, Status, and custom session fields) and explain how combining them with submission-status filters works.
